title: Thursday, August 20, 2026

headline.title: Two retail-scale gaps in opposite directions, and both of them kept going. WMT lost 9.15% — opening 106.38 after a 114.30 close, trading down to 102.85, and finishing 103.84 near the low on 83.6M shares, more than double its prior session. DE gained 6.94%, opening 611.12 and running to a 639.00 high before closing 620.94. The morning note had both: WMT as an outside day resolving down through the gap, DE as a 2 Down completing a 2-2 reversal up.
headline.summary: Underneath the two gaps the tape was heavy and narrow. SPY −0.84%, QQQ −0.72%, IWM −1.34%, and only three of twelve sectors closed green — SMH +0.31%, XLE +0.27%, XLRE +0.20% — none of them by more than a third of a percent. Health care was the worst at XLV −1.87%, with discretionary and staples behind it. The crypto complex was the loud exception: bitcoin ran past $68,000 overnight and printed $71,975, a roughly $1.44B short squeeze, dragging MSTR and COIN with it.

what_happened: WMT's gap was the whole story and it never bounced.

It beat on EPS and revenue, missed on US comps, and guided Q3 under consensus — and the market traded the guide. Wednesday had engulfed Tuesday on both sides, a genuine outside bar, and the gap resolved it down. Opened 106.38 against a 114.30 close, made its high at 107.00 in the first minutes, and spent the rest of the session grinding to a 102.85 low before closing 103.84. 83.6M shares against 34.3M the day before. There was no point in the session where the gap was being bought.
DE was the mirror image, and the 2-2 reversal completed on the same bar it triggered.

EPS $5.10 against $4.70, and management calling 2026 the bottom of the ag cycle. Wednesday had taken Tuesday's low without its high — a clean 2 Down — and the reversal needed the gap to hold. It did: opened 611.12, well above Wednesday's 596.06 high, ran to 639.00, and closed 620.94, +6.94%. The session low of 586.475 came early and never threatened the prior close.
The index was weak and the breadth was worse.

Three of twelve sectors green and none above +0.31%; nine red with XLV −1.87%, XLY −1.61% and XLP −1.41% at the bottom. IWM −1.34% underperformed SPY by half a percent. On a day with two 7-9% single-name moves in opposite directions, the index still could not find a bid, which says the dispersion was idiosyncratic rather than a rotation anyone was funding.

An outside bar with a directional catalyst is the one gap structure that tends not to fade, and this one did not offer a single hour of doubt.

Note the low did dip under the trigger level intraday — the structure survived because the close, not the path, defines a 2-2. It closed eighteen points off the high, which is the one blemish.
Bearish kicker. Cloud accelerating 45% but capex up 75%. Wednesday was a 2 Up closing near its high; premarket sits below the entire candle at 121.29 against Wed L 127.54.

The setup was correct at 8:30am and wrong by the close. It opened 123.47 — below Wednesday's entire range, exactly as described — fell to 121.88, and then reversed for the rest of the session to close 130.53, above Wednesday's 129.50 high and +1.26% on the day. A bearish kicker that closes above the candle it was supposed to reject is a full failure, and the reversal was +7.1% off the low on 28.1M shares.

how_played_out: Both retail gaps were called and both ran the full session in the called direction.

WMT was described as an outside bar resolving down through the gap, and it opened 106.38, topped at 107.00 within minutes, and closed 103.84 near a 102.85 low on more than double its average volume. DE was described as a 2 Down completing a 2-2 reversal, and it opened fifteen points clear of Wednesday's high, ran to 639.00, and closed +6.94%. Neither required a decision after the bell — but unlike most gap days this week, neither faded either.
BABA is the one to sit with, because the premarket description was correct and the conclusion was not.

The note said “premarket sits below the entire candle” and that was true at 8:30am and true again at the open, which printed 123.47 against Wednesday's 127.54 low. It then fell to 121.88 — a further 1.3% in the setup's favour — before reversing every hour to close 130.53, above Wednesday's high. +7.1% off the low. Cloud accelerating 45% against capex up 75% was read as a negative before the open and as growth by the close. The chart description was accurate; the interpretation of what the market would do with it was the error.
The semi breakdown failed at the opening print, which was knowable in the first minute.

SMH was flagged as a 2 Down with premarket at 555.02, under Wednesday's 556.315 low. It opened 559.375 — three dollars above that low — which invalidated the structure before a single bar completed. It closed 562.65, green, and was one of only three green sectors on the board. A breakdown setup whose premarket level is not held at the open is not a slow failure; it is a same-minute one, and it should come off the sheet rather than be carried.
Breadth was the day's real signal and none of the setups were positioned for it.

Nine of twelve sectors red, the three green ones up a combined less than 1%, and IWM −1.34% against SPY −0.84%. The book was three single-name gap trades and two sector calls, which meant the day's most reliable observation — that everything except two gaps was being sold — had no expression in it. The two gaps paid; the tape underneath them was ignored.

darkpool.note: No FlowMS board is on file for this session. This report was reconstructed from the broker's settled prices and the morning report's own published levels; the institutional flow board for 8/20 was not captured in the archive at the time, so there is nothing to grade here rather than an empty result. Where a board does exist for a session, this panel carries it. Treating the absence as “no flow” would be the wrong read — it is simply not recorded.

lessons: An outside bar with a guidance catalyst is the gap that does not fade.

WMT engulfed the prior session on both sides and then gapped down through it on a guidance miss, and it never traded back toward the gap — high in the first minutes, close near the low, volume 2.4× normal. That is a different animal from an earnings gap on a beat, which spent this whole stretch mean-reverting. The distinction worth carrying is what the gap is resolving: an outside bar has no defined direction until something resolves it, and a guidance cut resolves it decisively.
A correct chart description is not a correct call.

BABA's premarket write-up was accurate in every particular — 2 Up Wednesday closing near the high, premarket below the entire candle — and the stock closed above Wednesday's high, +1.26%, having rallied 7.1% off its low. The structure said one thing and the flow said another, and the note had no read on the flow. Describing the candle correctly and predicting the session are separate skills, and this report has been conflating them.
A breakdown that is not held at the opening print is over in the first minute.

SMH's premarket sat below Wednesday's low and it opened three dollars above it. That is not a setup that decays through the day — it is invalidated on the opening auction, and every hour it was still on the sheet after that was an hour of carrying a thesis the tape had already answered. Worth an explicit rule: a level-based breakdown gets checked against the opening print, not the close.
Two big winners can coexist with a book that missed the day.

WMT and DE were both right and both large. Meanwhile nine of twelve sectors fell, IWM lost 1.34%, and the three green sectors managed +0.31% between the best of them. The setups captured two idiosyncratic gaps and had nothing to say about the broad tape, which was the more persistent fact. A sheet of gap trades is not a view on the market, and on this day the difference mattered.
tomorrow: Closed 130.53, above Wednesday's 129.50 high after reversing 7.1% off a 121.88 low. The failed bearish kicker is now a completed reversal, and 129.50 is the level it has to hold for that to mean anything.

Closed 103.84 near a 102.85 low, −9.15% on 83.6M shares. After a gap of that size the first thing to watch is whether 102.85 holds — a failed retest of the low is the usual first tradeable structure, not the gap itself.

The 2 Down breakdown failed at the open and it closed 562.65, green, one of only three green sectors. If semis lead out of a session this weak across everything else, that divergence is the thing to follow rather than the index.

Breadth is the open question. Nine of twelve sectors red with the three green ones barely positive, and IWM underperforming SPY by half a percent. Either tomorrow broadens or this was distribution dressed as a quiet index day.

Bitcoin past $68,000 and a print at $71,975 set off roughly a $1.44B short squeeze, carrying MSTR and COIN with it. The equity proxies move faster than spot in both directions — worth watching whether the squeeze extends or unwinds into the weekend.

Ahead: Jackson Hole on 8/28, with Warsh delivering his first keynote as Chair — the first policy framing from a new Chair rather than a restatement of a known one. Everything between here and there is positioning.

tts.text: Grading the morning calls. Walmart was described as an outside bar resolving down through the gap, and that is exactly what it did. It opened one oh six thirty eight, printed its high of one oh seven within minutes, and never traded back toward the gap, closing one oh three eighty four near a one oh two eighty five low. Deere was described as a two down completing a two two reversal up, and it opened fifteen points clear of Wednesday's high, ran to six thirty nine, and closed up six point nine four percent. Alibaba was the failure and it is the instructive one. The note said the premarket sits below the entire candle, which was true at eight thirty and true again at the open of one twenty three forty seven. It then fell to one twenty one eighty eight and reversed every hour after that to close one thirty fifty three, above Wednesday's high, up seven point one percent off the low. Semis also failed. tts.label: Lessons
tts.text: Four things to carry forward. First, an outside bar with a guidance catalyst is the gap that does not fade. Walmart engulfed the prior session on both sides and then gapped down through it on a guidance miss, and it never looked back. That is a different animal from an earnings gap on a beat. Second, a correct chart description is not a correct call. Alibaba's write up was accurate in every particular and the stock closed above the candle it was supposed to reject. Third, a breakdown that is not held at the opening print is over in the first minute. Semis opened three dollars above the low the setup required, and every hour it stayed on the sheet after that was carrying a thesis the tape had already answered. Fourth, two big winners can coexist with a book that missed the day. Walmart and Deere were both right and both large, while nine of twelve sectors fell and small caps underperformed by half a percent. A sheet of gap trades is not a view on the market.
